purpose: Record targeted closure after the all-option first pass without rewriting the historical first-pass artifacts.

changes.reason: AQA's reference-only top-down/bottom-up alignment can be mapped to rights-clear subject evidence for pre-existing typology-based profiling versus data-driven behavioural/geographical profiling without reusing AQA teaching prose.

A CC BY 2026 criminal-justice study explicitly discusses minimisation and justification of offending behaviour, completing the previously missing named cognitive-distortion element alongside already accepted Eysenck, moral-reasoning, hostile-attribution and differential-association evidence.

Psychological effects of custody are now directly supported by CC BY 4.0 evidence. Token economy in a custodial/forensic setting remains rights-incomplete because the closest 2026 article is described as Creative Commons open access but the exact commercial-compatible licence flavour was not verified in accessible metadata.

The six-stage model is easy to identify factually, but the convenient explanatory sources inspected remain non-commercial. PubMed/original-article records are retained as factual leads, not promoted to OPEN reusable corpus without a rights-safe route.

interpretation: Targeted searching can close specialist option residuals without broad regeneration, but rights verification can become the bottleneck even where highly relevant material is publicly visible.
